name: a-person-is-made
asks: Can somebody arrive, become a person, and be handed their opening money without any of it appearing from nowhere?

steps.says: A new account has nobody yet, and asking is not an error.
The first person this account has ever had.

A name goes into chat, onto an ID card and into a database. Digits are not a name -- and it is the command's own declaration that refuses it, before any handler runs, which is why the code is bad_args and not bad_name.
She exists, she is not being played, and her opening money is exactly five hundred.
Selecting who you are already being is not an error. It is the same request twice, and it answers the same way.
One account plays one person at a time. Two live copies of one wallet is how money gets spent twice, so switching without letting go is refused.
Letting go is the way to switch.
And back, with everything she had still hers.
Everything a heads-up display needs, in one read that changes nothing.
She is carrying a phone and nothing else. Nobody handed it to her: the phone system listens for character.created and issues one, which is why the city can reach her before she has done anything.
